PullRequest.Title: chat: Add draft handoff and parallel-work invitation for Agents
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Make the move from editor Chat to the Agents Window preserve unfinished work, and invite Agent Host users to run tasks in parallel.

- Copy the current prompt, attachments, and source workspace from new, unsent normal Chat views/editors across the applicable Open Agents entry points. Preserve explicit caller targets and existing persisted-session reveal behavior; never clear the source or automatically send.
- Fill only an empty destination composer. Preserve existing text/attachments and its workspace/provider, and let newer edits, navigation, sends, or opening intents win. Keep unresolved remote workspace intent instead of falling back to an unrelated project.
- Add an Agent Host-only parallel-work invitation when another Agent Host session in the editor Sessions list is actively running. Exactly one widget owns the banner, including duplicate views of the same chat. Its button always captures that owner's current draft; X dismisses the chat until reload and Ignore persistently disables the invitation.
- Add independent experiment-controllable transfer and invitation toggles, enabled by default on Insiders and disabled on Stable/Code OSS. Read title/body directly from `chatAgentsParallelWorkBannerTitle` and `chatAgentsParallelWorkBannerDescription` treatments, with localized defaults.
- Preserve URI/image attachments and snapshot untitled-file contents into portable context, including attachment-only sendability. Reuse the notification primitive and existing draft persistence, with updated accessibility help.

## Validation

- Full `npm run compile`, including built-in extensions
- Staged-file hygiene via `node build/hygiene.ts`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- **299 passing focused Electron unit tests**, including destination consumption of unsaved attachments, workspace/provider delays, source/destination preservation, independent flags, direct treatments, single-widget rendering, dismissal/reload, stale actions, and accessibility
- `git diff --check`
- Launched Code OSS from this worktree and verified that the workbench loaded. A live multi-window handoff flow was not manually exercised.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous call path, full-model reads, base64 conversion, JSON allocation, and placement before the native open call are explicit. Exact pause duration varies with attachment sizes and hardware, which limits severity rather than confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: UI-thread CPU plus transient strings and bytes created while snapshotting models, base64-encoding images, and JSON-serializing the complete attachment collection
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows linearly with total attachment payload bytes; untitled models are copied in full with no size bound, and image entries are synchronously base64-encoded (4/3 expansion) before the entire collection is stringified.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: The Open Agents action can block the source renderer and delay window creation while producing large transient allocations and GC pressure.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Opening the Agents Window forwarded only workspace/session URI metadata, so it could call the native window service without reading full text models or encoding attachment payloads.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new handoff maps every attachment, snapshots complete untitled models via getValue(), exports binary entries to base64, and synchronously stringifies the resulting collection before the caller can invoke nativeHostService.openAgentsWindow.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added line 68 creates a single JSON string for the entire newly captured attachment set; this serialization did not exist on any Agents Window open path before the PR.
Findings.Title: Bound draft serialization before opening the Agents Window
Findings.Impact: A realistic draft containing a large unsaved log or several accepted image attachments makes the Open Agents click synchronously copy and encode tens of megabytes before the window begins opening, causing a visible pause and potentially a large memory spike.
Findings.Evidence: serializeChatDraft synchronously calls model.getValue()/getValueInRange for untitled resources, IChatRequestVariableEntry.toExport for each remaining attachment, and stringify for the full array at line 68. toExport base64-encodes Uint8Array values synchronously. captureDraftHandoffOptions calls this directly on the command path before openAgentsWindow; image attachment loading accepts files up to 30 MB, and untitled snapshots have no bound.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep large bytes in a buffer-aware IPC representation and transfer the draft after window opening has begun, rather than base64/stringifying it on the source UI thread. Also enforce a total handoff payload bound (surfacing the existing retained-source warning when exceeded) so untitled documents and multiple images cannot create an unbounded synchronous snapshot.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The event subscription, synchronous call graph, unconditional catalog getter, and getter allocation/deduplication are directly visible. Only the exact user-visible duration depends on catalog size and local event frequency.
Findings.PerformanceResource: UI-thread full-catalog array allocations, URI deduplication passes, session predicate checks, and resulting garbage
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each global context-key event costs O(N) in the complete active-and-archived session catalog; focus/add events can perform the same scan twice through _onSessionChanged followed by _update, and cost grows with retained session history.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Routine context/focus churn increasingly consumes CPU and creates GC pressure for users with large session histories, risking workbench interaction jank even when the banner owner has not changed.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: There was no parallel-work contribution listening to every context-key change, and Agents Window invitation state did not require materializing and deduplicating the full session catalog on those events.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added unfiltered global context listener calls _update; _updateOwner calls hasRunningAgentHostSession, whose model.sessions access allocates Array.from(_sessions.values()) and runs the migrated-session dedupe pass before .some can test status. _onSessionChanged also calls the same helper and then _update, duplicating the catalog pass for a new focus/session.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The PR adds the line-718 global listener and the new _update path that performs the full session-catalog read for each event; this repeated work was absent before the new contribution.
Findings.Title: Cache running-session state instead of rescanning on every context change
Findings.Impact: With hundreds or thousands of accumulated active and archived sessions, unrelated context-key updates and ordinary chat focus transitions repeatedly traverse and allocate the entire catalog although the running-session boolean changes only on session-model events.
Findings.Evidence: Line 718 subscribes to all context-key changes. The added hasRunningAgentHostSession helper at line 83 reads service.model.sessions; AgentSessionsModel.sessions constructs a new array and dedupes all entries on every read. _updateOwner invokes it unconditionally whenever the feature is enabled, and _onSessionChanged invokes it once more before calling _update.
Findings.Recommendation: Compute and cache hasRunningAgentHostSession when onDidChangeSessions fires, then let context/widget updates read that O(1) value. Filter context-key notifications to the keys used by the precondition, and reuse the cached result inside _onSessionChanged/_update to avoid the duplicate scan.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Agents Window from a new unsent chat through the command, title action, or parallel-work banner
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The source renderer synchronously captures text and attachments, snapshots untitled models, exports binary attachments, and stringifies the full draft before nativeHostService.openAgentsWindow can begin. The native open RPC and target-window IPC must then complete before the destination can consume the draft.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the native openAgentsWindow service from the source renderer with the serialized draft payload
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One renderer-to-main call per user invocation; the entire draft is included once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same open boundary carried only small workspace/session metadata; the PR adds the potentially large draft payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocked behind synchronous draft materialization and required to start/focus the Agents Window.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send vscode:selectAgentsFolder and the serialized draft from the main process to the destination renderer
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sendWhenReady call per successful window open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The channel already sent workspace/session selection metadata, but did not carry prompt, full text snapshots, or encoded image data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Destination restoration cannot apply the handoff until this message arrives and is parsed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total prompt/attachment bytes, especially full untitled model contents and resized image bytes; image count can reach model limits of 10/20 and is not UI-bounded for other models.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One capture is synchronous per invocation. Repeated opens are independent and can overlap only after each synchronous capture; renderer-to-main open calls are not coalesced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No snapshot or encoded-payload cache is used, intentionally capturing click-time content. Cold and warm Agents Window opens both rebuild and serialize the complete draft.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the full synchronous snapshot/base64/stringify path and its ordering before the native open call are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical prompts are small, but accepted images can originate from files up to 30 MB and untitled model snapshots have no total-size bound; exact pause and peak memory depend on payload and hardware.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable serialization/allocation regression because the new feature places unbounded payload construction on the click-to-window-open critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Receive a draft in the Agents Window and apply it to the empty New Session composer
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The target receives the IPC, waits for setup/restored lifecycle, resolves the requested workspace provider, opens at most one new provider session when needed, parses/revives attachments, and applies them only after the composer is ready.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/open the provider-backed New Session for the requested workspace before applying the draft
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one provider session creation per accepted draft handoff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A draft handoff did not exist; ordinary workspace selection could create a session separately, but no incoming draft waited on this creation path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before workspace selection and draft application; provider-specific implementations may cross IPC, subprocess, or network boundaries.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One incoming draft, one workspace, attachment count/bytes already serialized by the source, and up to the 15-second provider/view readiness window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One handoff intent is active; a newer intent cancels the prior one. Provider/session creation is awaited and performed at most once after provider readiness; readiness polling is serialized.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Mounted composer state is checked directly; when unmounted, persisted workspace draft state is read from storage. No cache is needed for the one-shot incoming draft, and newer input/navigation cancels it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the one-shot awaited creation and cancellation flow are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider startup cost varies by provider and workspace, but it is single-flight, cancellation-aware, and bounded by the handoff timeout.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the expensive provider operation is limited to one, preserves ordering, and is cancelled when newer user intent wins.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show and maintain the parallel-work invitation while Agent Host sessions and chat widgets change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The contribution displays defaults immediately, asynchronously resolves two treatment strings, and synchronously recomputes ownership on widget, session, configuration, and global context-key events.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve title and description experiment treatments through the assignment service/TAS client
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two concurrent lookups at contribution startup and two per assignment-refetch event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These two treatment lookups did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the initial rendering critical path because localized defaults are posted immediately; resolved copy causes a later update.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Complete active-and-archived Agent Sessions catalog size plus visible/recent chat widget count, multiplied by context/session/focus event frequency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Treatment lookups run as two concurrent promises per startup/refetch with stale-result suppression. Ownership updates are synchronous and guarded only against reentrancy, not coalesced across successive events.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: TAS can serve persisted/cached treatments while initial network setup is pending. Widget eligibility/dismissal is retained in in-memory sets. The running-Agent-Host predicate is not cached and rematerializes/deduplicates the full session catalog on each update.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the broad event listeners, uncached model.sessions getter, full dedupe pass, and duplicate focus-path scan are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of context-key events and catalog size varies by user, but the O(N) allocation/dedupe work on every event is deterministic and archived histories can accumulate substantially.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-work regression; cache the running-session state on session-model changes and use O(1) reads for unrelated context/widget events.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 45 changed files. Submitted two findings: synchronous unbounded draft serialization on the window-open path, and repeated full session-catalog materialization/deduplication on broad context events. Checked IPC payload flow, provider session creation, TAS lookups, cancellation, storage fallback, listener cleanup, collection retention, and cache/concurrency behavior; no other high-confidence performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
